tools.name: validate_problem
tools.description:
Check dimensions, bounds, and linear controllability before a solve.

This is POST /v1/validate and stays free when payment enforcement is on.
It does not use X-API-Key and it does not return HTTP 402. Call it before
solve_mpc when you want the plant rejected without spending a credit.

tools.name: solve_mpc
tools.description:
Solve a multi-step constrained MPC problem on the server.

Use this when the horizon has soft state bounds, hard input and slew limits,
and an offset-free disturbance rejection term. Pass the same ``session_id``
on later calls of one closed loop so the shifted primal and dual warm start
is restored.

tools.name: reset_warm_start
tools.description:
Clear one session's shifted primal and dual.

Next ``solve_mpc`` / ``POST /v1/solve`` with this ``session_id`` is cold.
The compiled solver stays. Stateless calls omit ``session_id`` and already
clear warm-start memory, so they do not use this tool.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_problem, start_autotune_job · Private data: get_autotune_job · Public sink: identify_discrete_plant, validate_problem, solve_mpc, reset_warm_start, start_autotune_job, autotune_template · Destructive: solve_mpc, reset_warm_start.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_problem, start_autotune_job · Private data: get_autotune_job · Public sink: identify_discrete_plant, validate_problem, solve_mpc, reset_warm_start, start_autotune_job, autotune_template · Destructive: solve_mpc, reset_warm_start

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
